1.

The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 04.12.2022.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 04.12.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Bagepalli Police Station, near Hyderabad - Bengaluru NH-44 Road, in Paragodu cross, the Petitioner was riding unoffending Passion Pro Motor Cycle bearing M.V.C.No.385/2023 3 SCCH - 7 registration No.KA-40-L-4511 along with Sri. Narasimhappa as a pillion rider to approach Paragodu village and when the Petitioner was proceeding at Paragodu cross and crossing the Bengaluru - Hyderabad NH-44 Road, the accused/driver of the offending Innova Car bearing registration No.KA-04-C- 8251 drove the same in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/ Petitioner and pillion rider of the unoffending vehicle fell down on the road and Petitioner/ PW-1 sustained grievous injuries on his right leg and pillion rider sustained simple injuries.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government General Hospital, Bagepalli for treatment and underwent surgery therein.
Thereafter, Petitioner given statement/ complaint before the Bagepalli police while under treatment.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.573/2022 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

Further it is alleged that prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale and healthy M.V.C.No.385/2023 4 SCCH - 7 and he was aged about 40 years and he was doing agriculture work and earning an income of Rs.500/- per day.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he became permanently disabled and he is unable to do his work normally as he was doing prior to the occurrence of the alleged accident.

The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Innova Car bearing registration No.KA-04-C-8251 and Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the RC owner of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.

sentences.text: In response to the notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 are appeared through their counsels and filed their respective written statements.

4. In the written statement of Respondent No.1, the Insurance Company has admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioner has not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it is denied having insured the vehicle involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents in accordance with law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and further the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. Act., and the driver of the offending car did not possess the valid and effective driving licence as on the date of occurrence of the accident and violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

5. In the written statement of respondent No.2, he admitted that he is the owner of the offending vehicle M.V.C.No.385/2023 6 SCCH - 7 and denied the petition averments in part including age,
avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No.1/Insurance company and policy was in force as on the date of accident, hence Respondent No.1 has to indemnify the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petitions.
6. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.

:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether petitioner proves that in this accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Innova Car bearing registration No.KA-04-C-8251 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the petitioner proves that age and earnings of the petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
(4) What order or award?

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government General Hospital, Bagepalli for treatment and underwent surgery therein.
It is contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The Respondent No.1/Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the injured Petitioner and the said Petitioner negligently and suddenly crossed the road with taking note of the approaching the offending vehicle.
There is every possibility of dashing against the offending vehicle without the driver becoming aware of it.
The driver of the offending vehicle cannot save accident, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be M.V.C.No.385/2023 9 SCCH - 7 held to be negligent.
The alleged accident occurred due to negligent and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it is alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident and violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

the Petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and he has M.V.C.No.385/2023 10 SCCH - 7 reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.11 documents.

I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex.P-1 is the True copy of FIR in Cr. No.573/2022, Ex.P-2 is the True copy of Statement/complaint dated 04.12.2022, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar dated 05.12.2022, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the Motor vehicle Accident Report, Ex.P.6 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.7 is the Charge Sheet,

Further he has denied that he has obtained free treatment therein.

Further he has deposed that he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards his medical expenditure and in that regard he will produce the documents and denied that he has not spent such amount towards his medical expenditure.

Further he M.V.C.No.385/2023 11 SCCH - 7 denied that he has not sustained any fracture and he has not underwent surgery in that regard and in the intention to get more compensation he has created concocted Ex.P-10 and Ex.P-11 documents and also purposefully modified the dates in the Hospital records.

Further he has denied that the offending car is not involved in the alleged accident and in the malafide intention and in collusion with the police and to get compensation they have falsely implicated the offending car and they have filed false case against the driver of the offending car
as such the Respondent No.1 Insurance Company is not M.V.C.No.385/2023 12 SCCH - 7 liable to pay any compensation and he has produced concocted created documents and he is deposing falsely.

Petitioner sustained grievous injury due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, MVA Report, Wound Certificate, Charge Sheet, Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to the M.V.C.No.385/2023 15 SCCH - 7 Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle, as a result rider/Petitioner of the unoffending vehicle sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Statement/Complaint, Ex.P3/Spot Mahazar, M.V.C.No.385/2023 16 SCCH - 7 Ex.P4/Spot sketch, Ex.P5/MVA Report, Ex.P-6/Wound Certificate, Ex.P-7/Charge Sheet, Ex.P8/Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P9/reply to Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act and Ex.P-10 & Ex.P-11/Discharge Summaries clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot shown in the Ex.P-4/Spot Sketch.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate and Ex.P-10/Discharge Summary would be caused by a road traffic accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused/driver.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent person/Petitioner aforesaid, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged M.V.C.No.385/2023 17 SCCH - 7 accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2 and 3:-

The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that the injured Petitioner was aged about 40 years at the time of accident and he is doing agriculture work and earning Rs.500/- per day and the Petitioner has incurred Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

22. On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent No.1 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.500/- per day, the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.

sentences.text: The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 40 years and he was doing agriculture work and earning income Rs.500/- per day.
The petitioner relied on the Ex.P.6/ Wound Certificate of the Petitioner and wherein the age of the Petitioner is shown as 40 years.
Hence it is clear that on the strength of the Ex.P-6/ Wound Certificate as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 40 years.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 40 years.
24. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was doing agriculture work and earning income Rs.500/- per day.
But he has not produced any documents to prove the income of the Petitioner.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the Petitioner taken at Rs.14,750/-.
25.

To prove the percentage of disability sustained by the Petitioner, neither the Petitioner got examined his treated doctor, nor produced disability certificate, hence M.V.C.No.385/2023 19 SCCH - 7 the Petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head future loss of income on account of permanent disability.
26. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as agriculture while doing the said work and in the alleged accident the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bone mid 1/3rd.
The doctor opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.

The injuries shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.
27. The Petitioner contended that, due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he took treatment as an inpatient at General Hospital, Bagepalli and undergone surgery.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head transportation, nourishment and other charges.
28. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.88,500/- (Rs.14,750/- p.m, X 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.

Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is M.V.C.No.385/2023 21 SCCH - 7 fixed on the respondent No.1/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.1 is directed to the deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 and 3 are partly in the affirmative.
33. Issue No.4:

In view of the findings on the above issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,88,500/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Eighty Eight Thousand and Five Hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent No.1 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in M.V.C.No.385/2023 22 SCCH - 7 favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether petitioner proves that in this accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Innova Car bearing registration No.KA-04-C-8251 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the petitioner proves that age and earnings of the petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
(4) What order or award?
:REASONS:
10. Issue No.1:- This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act  1989 for seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the alleged accident.
11.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Respondent No.1/Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the injured Petitioner and the said Petitioner negligently and suddenly crossed the road with taking note of the approaching the offending vehicle.
As such the insurance Kothala Venkata Ramana Alias ... vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182529527/
4 company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.
As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.
The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 40 years and he was doing agriculture work and earning income Rs.500/- per day.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 40 years.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was doing agriculture work and earning income Rs.500/- per day.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head transportation, nourishment and other charges.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Kothala Venkata Ramana Alias ... vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182529527/
5 14.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle, as a result rider/Petitioner of the unoffending vehicle sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate and Ex.P-10/Discharge Summary would be caused by a road traffic accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused/driver.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent person/Petitioner aforesaid, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
But he has not produced any documents to prove the income of the Petitioner.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the Petitioner taken at Rs.14,750/-.
25.
To prove the percentage of disability sustained by the Petitioner, neither the Petitioner got examined his treated doctor, nor produced disability certificate, hence M.V.C.No.385/2023 19 SCCH - 7 the Petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head future loss of income on account of permanent disability.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.88,500/- (Rs.14,750/- p.m, X 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl. Compensation under different Amount in No. heads (Rs) 1 Pain and suffering,
mental agony 1,50,000-00 2 1,00,000-00 Transportation, nourishment and other charges 3 Loss of amenities 1,50,000-00 4 88,500-00 Loss of income during laid up period Total 4,88,500-00 31.
The Petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.4,88,500/-.
32.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is M.V.C.No.385/2023 21 SCCH - 7 fixed on the respondent No.1/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.1 is directed to the deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 and 3 are partly in the affirmative.
33. Issue No.4:
In view of the findings on the above issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,88,500/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Eighty Eight Thousand and Five Hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent No.1 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in M.V.C.No.385/2023 22 SCCH - 7 favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
